title: Analysis of biodiesel by high performance liquid chromatography using refractive index detector
author: Syed
materials: A High Performance Liquid Chromatographic system (HPLC Model- LC 20 AT Prominence, Shimadzu, Japan) fitted with Refractive index detector (RID-10A, Shimadzu, Japan) and millennium 32 system software was used to quantify the fatty acid methyl esters produced during reaction. Separations were carried out on a 238 nm in Luna C18 column of particle size 5 mm and (250 × 4.6 mm) I.D. Methanol mobile phase was filtered through a 0.45 μm membrane filter (Millipore), and then degassed ultrasonically prior to use. The flow rate was 1 mL min−1, the injection volume was 20 μL and the column oven temperature was maintained at 40 °C. Each component in the samples analyzed was identified by comparing its retention time with that of the respective standards. Quantification was carried out by integration of the peaks using external standards followed by calculating the% yield as weight of methyl esters produced to weight of oil initially taken [1].

steps.title: Configure HPLC system
steps.instruction: Set up the High Performance Liquid Chromatographic system (model LC‑20 AT Prominence, Shimadzu, Japan) equipped with a Refractive Index Detector (RID‑10A, Shimadzu) and control it with the Millennium 32 software.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phase
steps.instruction: Filter methanol mobile phase through a 0.45 µm Millipore membrane filter and degas it ultrasonically before use.

steps.title: Set HPLC operating parameters
steps.instruction: Install the Luna C18 column (particle size 5 µm, dimensions 250 × 4.6 mm I.D., operated at 238 nm), set the column oven to 40 °C, program a flow rate of 1 mL min⁻¹, and define an injection volume of 20 µL.

steps.title: Prepare standard solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve 40 mg of the reference standard in 2 mL methanol to make a stock solution (20 mg mL⁻¹). From this stock, prepare five serial dilutions with concentrations of 2, 4, 8, 12 and 16 mg mL⁻¹ using methanol as the solvent.

steps.title: Set baseline and run standards
steps.instruction: Set the HPLC baseline according to the program described in the analysis section, then inject 20 µL of each standard dilution, recording the corresponding peak‑area values.

steps.title: Identify sample components
steps.instruction: Inject the biodiesel samples (20 µL) and identify each component by comparing its retention time with those of the respective standards.

steps.title: Quantify methyl esters and calculate yield
steps.instruction: Integrate the peaks using external standard calibration curves (peak area vs concentration for each methyl ester) and calculate the % yield as (weight of methyl esters produced ÷ weight of oil initially taken) × 100.
